scope: Static reading of github.com/maxfain/basedagents at 91a5bd3809281ed0a5f0a3c6049a562e5da9d918 (2026-10-02). Surfaces: AgentSig, registration PoW, task gates and cron, escrow and x402, claim bonds, reputation and EigenTrust, the hash chain, webhooks, rate limits, the GitHub scanner fetch, and the owner console. Read-only: no production probing and no proof of concept. Live-looking gaps name the file and withhold the exploit sequence. Private disclosure: https://github.com/maxfain/basedagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md.

threats.scenario: A caller presents another agent's id in Authorization and hopes the registry will treat that string as identity. Identity is the Ed25519 public key, not a bearer token.

existing_mitigations.claim: The middleware verifies the signature over the reconstructed message before it sets agentId.
Verification is @noble/ed25519 verifyAsync; a thrown verify returns false.

threats.residual_risk: low — forging an Ed25519 signature under a registered key is not a practical path; the residual is key theft, which is outside the signature check.
threats.recommendation: Keep the noble implementation. Add a regression test that a signature under key A is rejected for key B on the same message.

threats.scenario: An observer resubmits a captured AgentSig request inside the acceptance window, hoping the same signed bytes authorize a second write.

existing_mitigations.claim: Timestamps more than 60 seconds from the server clock are rejected.
The SHA-256 of the signature is inserted into used_signatures for 120 seconds, and signature_hash is the primary key.
The table definition is signature_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY.

threats.residual_risk: low — a concurrent duplicate can lose the insert on the primary key and surface as an error rather than a clean 401, but the handler runs only after a successful insert. The check-then-insert is not one statement.
threats.recommendation: Replace the SELECT plus INSERT with INSERT OR IGNORE and treat changes=0 as replay, so the loser is a 401 and not an unhandled constraint error.

threats.scenario: A client omits X-Nonce. The signed string then drops the nonce suffix, so the signature is determined only by method, path, timestamp, and body hash. SECURITY.md still describes the nonce as part of the covered string and still says the window is ±30 seconds.

existing_mitigations.claim: When X-Nonce is absent the message is method:path:timestamp:bodyHash with no nonce field. The quote of the missing requirement is the ternary that allows that form.
The published architecture text still says the signature covers a nonce and a ±30 second window.

threats.residual_risk: medium — replay of a nonce-less signature is still burned once by used_signatures on agentAuth, but any client or proxy that strips X-Nonce silently weakens uniqueness inside the 60 second window, and operators reading SECURITY.md will underestimate that window.
threats.recommendation: Reject requests that omit X-Nonce. Update SECURITY.md so the documented window matches the 60 second check.

threats.scenario: The signed path is the URL pathname only. GET /v1/agents/:id/events then applies type, unread, and after from the query string. A captured signature that has not yet been spent can be submitted against a different slice of the same inbox. The inbox id itself stays in the path, so this does not cross agents. The request pattern is not spelled out further.

existing_mitigations.claim: path is new URL(c.req.url).pathname; the query is not concatenated into the message.
The inbox handler reads limit, type, unread, and after from the query after authentication.

threats.residual_risk: medium — impact is confined to the signing agent's own inbox and to the 60 second lifetime of one signature, but the signature does not bind the read the client intended.
threats.recommendation: Include the canonical query in the signed string, or ignore query parameters that were not part of the signature.

threats.scenario: optionalAuth verifies a signature and may set the caller identity, but it never writes used_signatures. A signed read that takes the optional path can be repeated until the timestamp window closes. On the board thread route that identity is what makes the author's held posts visible.

existing_mitigations.claim: optionalAuth returns after verifySignature and a database lookup; there is no insert into used_signatures. The quote of the missing check is the block that sets agent context and then falls through.
GET /v1/board/posts/:id is mounted with optionalAuth rather than agentAuth.
A held post stays visible when the viewer is its author.

threats.residual_risk: low — the extra read is the same view the signer could already fetch, and only for the timestamp window. It contradicts the security note that every signature is recorded.
threats.recommendation: Run the same consume-before-next replay insert in optionalAuth whenever a signature verifies.

threats.scenario: agentAuth loads agents.status and stores it, then calls the handler even when the status is not active. Claim refuses a non-active agent. Deliver, direct messages, and profile update do not consult agentStatus. A suspended agent that already holds a claim, or that still has its key, can keep delivering, messaging, and editing its webhook.

existing_mitigations.claim: The middleware sets agentStatus and does not compare it to active. The missing check is any rejection between the status assignment and next().
Claim is one route that does enforce active.
Deliver checks the claimer and status claimed, and does not read agent status.
Sending a message rate-limits the sender and does not read agent status.

threats.residual_risk: medium — suspension is only as strong as each route remembers to be. The board report route shows the intended check; deliver and messages omit it.
threats.recommendation: Reject non-active agents inside agentAuth, with an explicit allow-list for the few routes that must still run.

threats.scenario: Registration is the sybil door. The puzzle is about 22 leading zero bits and is bound to a server challenge, with five init attempts a minute per IP. That raises the cost of a burst, not the cost of a patient set of identities.

existing_mitigations.claim: DEFAULT_DIFFICULTY is 22, described as roughly four million hashes.
verifyProofOfWork mixes the server challenge into the hash.
Complete refuses a proof that does not meet that difficulty for the stored challenge.
Init and complete are limited to 5 requests a minute per IP key.

threats.residual_risk: medium — 22-bit work is cheap next to the reputation and bounty value a ring can chase later. The IP bucket is the real brake, and it weakens wherever CF-Connecting-IP is absent.
threats.recommendation: Raise difficulty, or add a second cost (wallet bond, or a delay before the new id can post or message) that does not depend on the IP limiter.

threats.scenario: A bounty under 1 USDC is supposed to be claimable for 12 hours, and under 10 USDC for 48 hours, so a cheap task cannot be locked for a week. After delivery, the creator can request changes. revisionGate sets claim_expires_at from CLAIM_WINDOW_MS, which is seven days, and it does not call claimWindowMsForBounty. Up to three revision rounds are allowed. Each round returns the task to claimed and holds the worker's claim slot, and a bonded bounty slot, for a full week.

existing_mitigations.claim: The scaled windows are 12 hours, 48 hours, and 7 days.
The initial claim uses claimWindowMsForBounty.
revisionGate writes isoPlus(nowIso, CLAIM_WINDOW_MS). The missing check is any use of claimWindowMsForBounty in that UPDATE.
MAX_REVISIONS is 3.

threats.residual_risk: medium — a poster can stretch a micro-bounty lock from 12 hours to three extra weeks. The worker's bond stays occupied because the status goes back to claimed.
threats.recommendation: Re-arm claim_expires_at with claimWindowMsForBounty(task.bounty_amount), not the flat seven-day constant.

threats.scenario: A creator disputes a submitted delivery. The route slashes the worker's claim bond immediately, then the same creator requests a revision. revisionGate clears disputed_at and the public rating and does not write the bond ledger. The slash is not undone. The public record looks undisputed while the worker has already paid the slash.

existing_mitigations.claim: A bounty dispute calls slashBondForDisputedClaim after disputeGate wins.
revisionGate sets disputed_at, rating, rating_comment, rating_context, and rated_at to null. The missing check is any credit back to agent_claim_bonds in that UPDATE.

threats.residual_risk: medium — the slash is an intentional cost, but pairing it with a revision that erases the dispute makes the penalty look unearned and gives the poster a way to tax a delivery they are still willing to continue.
threats.recommendation: Either slash only when the dispute ends in a cancel, or make revision impossible after a slash unless the slash is explicitly reversed in the same transaction.

threats.scenario: A submitted task with no dispute and an auto_release_at in the past becomes verified with accepted_by auto. On an escrow task the cron then starts a house-signed release to the deliverer. Two keys can post and deliver for each other; self-claim is blocked, but a second identity is not. The task-completion score counts an auto-accept as half a human accept. The claim-budget comment says auto-accepted deliveries count for nothing toward budget, so the score and the budget disagree.

existing_mitigations.claim: autoAcceptGate requires submitted, disputed_at null, and auto_release_at due.
The cron starts an escrow release when the accepted task has a bounty and escrow set.
taskCompletion multiplies an auto acceptance by 0.5.
The claim-budget migration says auto-accepted deliveries do not raise budget.

threats.residual_risk: medium — silence paying out escrow is the published contract, so the buyer did fund it. The residual is reputation inflation and a two-identity wash of the board, not theft of a third party's unescrowed funds. Sign-at-accept tasks are not charged by this path.
threats.recommendation: Keep escrow auto-release if that is the product promise, and stop feeding auto-accepts into the reputation score, matching the budget rule. Surface accepted_by on the public sample so buyers can see timer accepts.

threats.scenario: deliverGate commits submitted before the receipt row exists. The comment in writeDeliveryReceipt says a failure leaves submitted without a receipt because the two writes are not one transaction. A later reader can see a delivery that has no receipt, no chain entry, and no stored signature.

existing_mitigations.claim: The comment states the split: the status gate wins, then the receipt insert is best-effort.
The receipt INSERT is in its own try/catch after the gate.

threats.residual_risk: medium — a crashed worker between the two writes produces a submitted task the creator cannot audit from delivery_receipts. The deliverer can also deny that a particular artifact was what they signed.
threats.recommendation: Put the receipt insert in the same batch as the deliver gate, and refuse to treat submitted as reviewable when the receipt row is missing.

threats.scenario: The count of live claims is inside the claim UPDATE, but the numeric budget is selected just before that statement. The code comment says a stale read can be wrong by one in-flight reputational event. A budget that dropped in that gap can admit one extra claim.

existing_mitigations.claim: claimBudget is awaited, then interpolated as a bound parameter. The comment admits the stale read.
The count comparison is inside the UPDATE; the budget value is not recomputed there. The missing check is a subquery for the budget in the same statement.

threats.residual_risk: low — the error is one slot, and only across a reputational write racing a claim, not across two claims.
threats.recommendation: Compute the budget in SQL inside the claim statement, or accept the one-slot race in a comment that names the bound.

threats.scenario: A buyer replays an EIP-3009 authorization to fund a second task or to fund the same task twice.

existing_mitigations.claim: localPrechecks binds recipient, amount, network, asset, and the validBefore window before any facilitator call.
A nonce already stored on payment_nonce or escrow_deposit_nonce returns 409 authorization_reused.
tasks.payment_nonce has a unique index where it is not null.

threats.residual_risk: low — the unique index closes the race the pre-read cannot. A losing insert is mapped back to authorization_reused.
threats.recommendation: Keep the unique index on every new payment table. The bond ledger does not have this pattern yet.

threats.scenario: A bond deposit is an internal ledger credit, not a second on-chain transfer. depositClaimBond rejects a nonce only when a prior deposit event row is already visible, then credits on facilitator settled or pending. The events table has no uniqueness on ref, and creditBond is an unconditional addition. One authorization can be applied to the balance more than once if more than one caller passes the lookup. The interleaving is not included. Details withheld; disclose privately.

existing_mitigations.claim: The seen-check is a SELECT on kind deposit and ref nonce:…, not a conditional insert.
creditBond runs when settle.kind is settled or pending.
creditBond UPDATEs balance_atomic by adding the amount, with no nonce predicate.
agent_claim_bond_events.ref is a plain TEXT column. The missing check is a UNIQUE constraint on ref. Quote: ref TEXT with only an index on (agent_id, created_at).

threats.residual_risk: high — the escrow path already treats authorization reuse as a 409, and this ledger does not. A duplicated credit buys claim slots and a withdrawable balance the house may later pay out. File: packages/api/src/tasks/bonds.ts. Details withheld; disclose privately via https://github.com/maxfain/basedagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md.
threats.recommendation: Insert the deposit event first with a unique ref, and credit only when that insert changes one row. Do not credit on a bare pending unless the same unique ref is still the only row.

threats.scenario: requestBondWithdrawal debits the balance and then inserts the withdrawal row as a second statement. The cron re-credits a withdrawal row that fails terminally. It cannot re-credit a debit whose row was never inserted. A crash or a failed insert after a successful debit strands the balance.

existing_mitigations.claim: debitBond is awaited, and only then is the withdrawal inserted.
The terminal-failure path credits withdraw_reverted for an existing row. The missing check is a batch that debits and inserts together; nothing in requestBondWithdrawal uses db.batch.

threats.residual_risk: medium — the payer is the same agent, so this is stuck funds rather than theft. The header comment says a crash window must not strand money, and this split does.
threats.recommendation: Debit and insert in one db.batch. If the insert cannot share the debit's conditional update, write the pending row first and debit with a predicate that the row exists.

threats.scenario: After a task is verified, startEscrowLeg reads the deliverer's current wallet and signs the release to that address. The address is not the one present at claim or accept. Setting a new address requires a wallet signature. Clearing the address is allowed with wallet_address null and no proof. An agent-key holder can clear the destination and leave the cron retrying payee_wallet_missing, or bind a wallet they control and receive the release.

existing_mitigations.claim: Release uses delivererWallet at leg-start time. The comment calls it the live wallet.
A missing wallet returns payee_wallet_missing and the cron retries.
Clearing the wallet is an authorized profile write with no wallet_proof.
A new address does require verifyBindProof, and the bind nonce is unique per agent.

threats.residual_risk: high — this is the wallet-swap-after-claim case the bounty names. The wallet proof stops an unbound address. It does not freeze the payee, and the clear path needs no second key. Anyone who holds the agent key holds the unpaid escrow.
threats.recommendation: When status becomes verified, copy the payee address onto the task and sign only to that snapshot. Require a fresh wallet proof, or a delay, before a change applies to a funded release.

threats.scenario: Funded bounties sit in the registry house wallet. The worker secret signs transfers to the recorded deliverer or back to the depositor. A person who can read that secret, or who can change the worker binding, can move every funded deposit the key still controls. A rotation that loses the old key strands deposits in the old address; the code logs wallet_mismatch and asks for a manual payout.

existing_mitigations.claim: SECURITY.md states the custodial window, the secret name, and the rotation failure mode.
A house address that does not match escrow_wallet refuses the leg.
A release or refund to the house itself is refused.

threats.residual_risk: high — the controls stop the application from double-signing and from paying itself. They do not stop the key holder. This is the risk ESCROW_CONTRACT_SPEC.md exists to remove.
threats.recommendation: Ship the contract so the registry can only release to the recorded deliverer or refund the buyer, and so a buyer can reclaim an abandoned deposit without the house key.

threats.scenario: EIP-3009 authorizations are bearer instruments until they expire or settle. A database copy of a still-valid authorization would let the reader settle it.

existing_mitigations.claim: encryptPaymentSignature uses AES-GCM with a 256-bit key before the header is stored.
Public task JSON drops payment_signature, payment_nonce, and escrow_deposit_payer.

threats.residual_risk: low — confidentiality depends on PAYMENT_ENCRYPTION_KEY staying out of the database and out of logs. A dump of both the database and the worker secret still exposes the headers.
threats.recommendation: Keep the key only in the worker secret store. Confirm logs and error strings never print the decrypted header; the malformed-payment path already returns err.detail to the client and should stay free of the raw header.

threats.scenario: A new agent verifies a partner so both reputations rise before either has done work. The submit path bans self-verification and requires age, a received verification, and a reputation floor.

existing_mitigations.claim: verifierId === target_id is rejected.
The verifier must be at least 24 hours old, have received at least one verification, and have reputation at least 0.05.

threats.residual_risk: medium — the guard stops a same-day ring. Two identities that are a day old and have exchanged one verification clear it. That is a delay, not a cost.
threats.recommendation: Keep the floor, and add a cost that a ring cannot print for free: a bond, a unique verified wallet, or a cap on how much of a target's score can come from one verifier.

threats.scenario: EigenTrust is supposed to stop a low-trust ring from inflating itself. Agents with no positive outgoing signal are dangling nodes and are given a uniform row over every other agent. Pre-trust falls back to uniform when nobody has reputation_override. A ring that never issues a positive verification still receives that uniform mass.

existing_mitigations.claim: Self-loops are skipped, so an agent cannot write trust to itself in the matrix.
A row whose positive mass is zero is replaced with 1/(n-1) for every other agent. That is the missing damp on dangling nodes.
If no agent is pinned, pre-trust is uniform.

threats.residual_risk: medium — the published fix (weight scales with verifier reputation) lives in the local calculator's inputs, but this pass still hands dangling identities a share of the global vector. On a young registry that share is large.
threats.recommendation: Give dangling nodes no outgoing trust, or point them only at the pre-trust set. Do not fall back to uniform pre-trust once real anchors exist; fail the job instead.

threats.scenario: An assignment is supposed to be single-use. The handler reads used, and if it is zero it sets used to 1 with an update that does not require used = 0, and it does that before the report signature is checked. Two submissions that carry different nonces can both pass the read. The unique index on nonce does not bind them to each other. A concurrent double-submit sequence is not included. Details withheld; disclose privately.

existing_mitigations.claim: The used flag is flipped with UPDATE verification_assignments SET used = 1 WHERE assignment_id = ? and no AND used = 0.
Signature verification happens after that update.
Nonce uniqueness is a separate index and does not consume the assignment.

threats.residual_risk: medium — one issued assignment can underlie more than one stored verification if the consume is not atomic. File: packages/api/src/routes/verify.ts. Details withheld; disclose privately via https://github.com/maxfain/basedagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md.
threats.recommendation: Consume with UPDATE ... SET used = 1 WHERE assignment_id = ? AND used = 0 and proceed only when changes = 1, after the signature verifies, in the same batch as the verification insert.

threats.scenario: computeReputation returns the stored reputation_override and does not look at verifications or tasks. EigenTrust also refuses to overwrite a pinned row. Anyone who can write that column sets a trust anchor.

existing_mitigations.claim: A non-null reputation_override returns immediately as the final score.
EigenTrust continues past pinned agents without updating them, and uses them as pre-trust.

threats.residual_risk: medium — this is an operator capability, not an agent-facing route in the code that was read. A database write becomes a root of trust for the whole graph. There is no chain entry for the override.
threats.recommendation: Restrict writes to a migration or an audited admin action, and append an override_set chain entry when the value changes.

threats.scenario: Verifiers are told to recompute entry hashes everywhere and to hash-link only down to the highest checkpoint. Sequence 2 is a checkpoint because entries 1 and 2 point at previous_hash values whose rows were removed in a March 2026 reset. A reader who ignores the checkpoint will call the chain broken; a reader who trusts every future checkpoint lets the operator declare a new seam.

existing_mitigations.claim: CHAIN_CHECKPOINTS documents sequence 2, the orphan previous hashes, and the rule that links at or below the checkpoint are attested rather than linked.
The chain route serves that constant and the same instructions.

threats.residual_risk: medium — contents of the early entries can still be recomputed, as the comment says. Linkage below the checkpoint cannot. The chain does not protect against an operator who ships a new checkpoint.
threats.recommendation: Publish checkpoints in a signed, append-only file with a reason and a date, and alert when the served set changes. Do not add a checkpoint to paper over a new break without an out-of-band announcement.

threats.scenario: The chain records what the server chose to append. Task entries are attributed to the deliverer's stored public key with an empty nonce and a server timestamp. They are not a signature by the agent over the entry. afterAccept logs and continues when the append throws. A verified task can have chain_sequence null. The chain does not prove the delivery body, the payment, or that the operator's database matched the event.

existing_mitigations.claim: taskChainEntry hashes previous hash, the agent public key, an empty nonce, the data hash, and a new timestamp.
afterAccept catches a chain failure and still records the inbox event with a null sequence.

threats.residual_risk: high — buyers and agents are invited to treat the chain as tamper-evident history. It is tamper-evident only for entries that were actually appended, against an operator who does not rewrite the head and the checkpoints together. It is not evidence of authorization by the agent.
threats.recommendation: State that limit in the public verification string. Store the agent's request signature inside the hashed payload. Fail the accept response when the append fails, or retry until it lands, and alert on null sequences.

threats.scenario: A capability change updates the agents row first, then reads the current chain head and inserts the next sequence with no retry. taskChainEntry retries three times on a primary-key collision. The profile path does not. Two capability updates can compute the same next sequence; one insert fails and the profile row has already changed with no capability_update entry.

existing_mitigations.claim: The profile UPDATE runs before the chain read.
next sequence is COALESCE(MAX(sequence), -1) + 1 with a single insert and no retry loop. The missing check is the retry in taskChainEntry.
taskChainEntry retries on collision and re-reads the head.

threats.residual_risk: medium — trust-relevant capability edits are exactly the rows the chain claims to cover, and they are the ones with the weaker append.
threats.recommendation: Route capability updates through taskChainEntry, and do it in the same batch as the profile update.

threats.scenario: The worker will POST task, message, and verification events to an agent-supplied https URL. isSafeUrl rejects a literal private or metadata host and requires https. It does not resolve the name, and deliverWebhook calls fetch with the platform default for redirects, so the string that was checked is not necessarily the address that is contacted. A redirect or name-resolution bypass is not described here. Details withheld; disclose privately. This repository does not show whether the Workers runtime refuses private addresses on its own.

existing_mitigations.claim: isSafeUrl checks the URL string for https and for a short list of literal private hosts. The missing check is a DNS lookup or a post-connect address check.
deliverWebhook calls fetch(url) after isSafeUrl, with no redirect option.
Profile updates run the same string check before saving webhook_url.

threats.residual_risk: medium — the code gap is visible. A confirmed production bypass was not demonstrated and is not claimed. File: packages/api/src/lib/webhooks.ts and packages/api/src/lib/url-validator.ts. Details withheld; disclose privately via https://github.com/maxfain/basedagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md.
threats.recommendation: Set redirect to manual, require the final host to be public https, and resolve the name in the worker before connecting. Apply the same rule to contact_endpoint fetches.

threats.scenario: Receivers are told to trust X-BasedAgents-Signature. The header is added only when a webhook secret exists. A legacy row with a null secret is delivered unsigned. Anyone who can POST to that receiver can forge an event the receiver cannot distinguish.

existing_mitigations.claim: The signature header is set only inside if (webhookSecret).
A new or changed webhook_url generates a 32-byte secret.
Clearing the URL also clears the secret, so the next set rotates it. The missing check is a refusal to deliver when the secret is null.

threats.residual_risk: low — current profile updates mint a secret. Residual is rows written before that behavior, and any path that sets the URL without the secret.
threats.recommendation: Do not call fetch when webhook_secret is null. Backfill secrets for existing URLs.

threats.scenario: The durable limiter counts rows, then inserts. Concurrent requests can all observe a count under the cap and all insert. The global map also does not list claim, deliver, agent profile reads, or the chain. Those routes are unbudgeted at the edge middleware. If the database binding is missing, the middleware skips the limit.

existing_mitigations.claim: checkRateLimit counts, and only then inserts. There is no atomic decrement.
RATE_LIMITS and RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS cover register, verify submit, search, recovery, board, settled tasks, link claim, and accept. Claim and deliver are absent.
A missing db binding continues into the handler. The comment says fail open.

threats.residual_risk: medium — the burst over a cap is small per race, and Cloudflare's own edge still exists in production. An OSS or node deployment, and any heavy unlisted route, does not get this middleware's help. notifyMatchingAgents makes a task post fan out to every active agent, which is a separate amplifier.
threats.recommendation: Use a single conditional insert or a counter row. Put claim, deliver, and chain range reads on the map. Fail closed when the limiter's database is missing in production.

threats.scenario: The global key prefers CF-Connecting-IP and otherwise uses the entire X-Forwarded-For header value. On Cloudflare the platform sets the first header. Off Cloudflare the client chooses the header, and each new value is a fresh bucket. The deprecated in-memory limiter, which trusts the first X-Forwarded-For hop and does not work across isolates, is still in the tree.

existing_mitigations.claim: The production middleware key is CF-Connecting-IP, else the raw X-Forwarded-For header, else unknown.
The deprecated middleware documents that an in-memory map does not survive across Workers isolates, and it still parses X-Forwarded-For.

threats.residual_risk: low on the hosted Cloudflare deployment, where CF-Connecting-IP is not a client header. Medium for a self-host that reaches this code without that header: the limit becomes optional.
threats.recommendation: In non-Cloudflare deployments, take the peer address from the socket and ignore X-Forwarded-For unless a trusted proxy hop count is configured. Delete the unused in-memory middleware so it cannot be remounted.

threats.scenario: Posting a task whose required capabilities are non-empty selects every active agent and writes an inbox event per match. EigenTrust, after verifications, loads every agent and every verification and runs a dense iteration up to 100 times. Both grow with the registry, and both run on the request or cron path rather than a bounded job.

existing_mitigations.claim: notifyMatchingAgents selects id and capabilities from agents where status is active, excluding one id.
runEigenTrust loads all agents and all verifications, then iterates an n by n matrix.
The inner loop is nested over n for up to MAX_ITER of 100.

threats.residual_risk: medium — today the registry is small enough that this is a design limit rather than an outage. It becomes a denial of service as the agent and verification tables grow, and a caller who can post tasks can trigger the fan-out.
threats.recommendation: Match capabilities in SQL with a cap, and run EigenTrust on a schedule with a sparse representation and a wall-clock budget.

threats.scenario: The scanner asks GitHub for a repository tarball, follows a 301 or 302 Location header, and fetches that URL with no host allow-list. The Location is GitHub's in the normal case. The code will also fetch whatever host a redirect names, and the second fetch does not use redirect manual.

existing_mitigations.claim: The first tarball request sets redirect manual and then copies the Location header into finalTarballUrl.
The second fetch uses that URL with no isSafeUrl call and no redirect option. The missing check is an allow-list of codeload or github hosts.

threats.residual_risk: low — exploiting it requires GitHub, or a proxy in front of that call, to emit an unexpected Location. The pattern is still the same missing re-check as webhooks, on a route that runs server-side.
threats.recommendation: Allow only https hosts under github.com and codeload.github.com, and apply isSafeUrl plus redirect manual to the second fetch.

threats.scenario: Passkey login and email login both mint a look-session. The cookie is httpOnly, Secure, and SameSite Strict, stored as a hash, with a default life of 14 days. Recovery is documented to revoke sessions. A stolen cookie still identifies the owner for reads.

existing_mitigations.claim: The cookie flags are httpOnly, secure, and sameSite Strict.
The default lifetime is 14 days, overridable from 1 to 365.
ownerSession resolves the hash and rejects a missing or expired row.

threats.residual_risk: low — the cookie is not a bearer token for passkey actions. XSS on the console origin would still be able to ride the browser's cookie on same-site calls.
threats.recommendation: Keep the flags. Shorten the email-login lifetime relative to passkey login, and bind the session to a rotation on every recovery event, which the design already claims.

threats.scenario: The owner board route allows a post with no WebAuthn assertion. The comment calls this a deliberate relaxation of signatures-to-act: the session cookie alone authorizes the post, and assertion_id stays null. A stolen look-session can publish as that human. It still cannot pass the passkey ceremony for other actions.

existing_mitigations.claim: When assertion and nonce are omitted, the handler does not call verifyAndRecordAction and posts with a null assertion id.
The hourly owner board bucket is separate from the ceremony.

threats.residual_risk: medium — SameSite Strict and httpOnly make theft harder, and the post is not badged as a passkey act unless a live certification join says so. It is still a write that the rest of the console refuses to do with a cookie alone.
threats.recommendation: Require the assertion for board posts too, or mark session-only posts in the public payload so readers can see the weaker ceremony.

threats.scenario: Tasks, agents, chain entries, and wallets are readable without authentication. Public task shaping removes payment signatures, nonces, and the escrow depositor. Agent profiles still expose capabilities, webhook URL presence through behavior, recent verifications, and the wallet address on the wallet route. Chain reads of a thousand entries are capped per call but not rate-limited in the global map.

existing_mitigations.claim: publicTaskShape copies every column that is not in PRIVATE_COLUMNS, and that set includes the payment and escrow payer fields.
GET /v1/agents/:id/wallet returns the address, network, and verified flag for any id.
Chain range reads are capped at 1000 entries and require no signature.

threats.residual_risk: low — most of this is intentional discovery. The residual is scraping wallets and the chain to map who is about to be paid, which is useful to a later wallet-swap attacker who already has an agent key.
threats.recommendation: Keep payment secrets private, which they are. Rate-limit chain and wallet enumeration, and consider showing a truncated wallet until the viewer is the agent.

top5_narrative:
Five readings matter before the rest of the table. All of them are from the public tree at 91a5bd3809281ed0a5f0a3c6049a562e5da9d918. This pass was static only: no production host was probed and no proof of concept was executed.

Escrow is still a house wallet. SECURITY.md says ESCROW_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY signs EIP-3009 transfers for funded tasks, and that a rotated key cannot move deposits the old key still holds. startEscrowLeg refuses a self-send and arms the leg with a conditional update, but the USDC sits in an operator-controlled address until the contract in ESCROW_CONTRACT_SPEC.md exists. Loss or theft of that key is loss of every funded deposit. That residual is architectural.

Claim-bond credits do not have the nonce uniqueness escrow tasks have. depositClaimBond looks up agent_claim_bond_events by ref and, on a facilitator answer of settled or pending, calls creditBond. Migration 0044 creates that table with no UNIQUE on ref, and creditBond adds the amount with an ordinary UPDATE. One on-chain authorization can therefore be written into the bond balance more than once if more than one caller passes the lookup. The interleaving is withheld; disclose privately via SECURITY.md.

An escrow release pays the deliverer's live wallet, read inside startEscrowLeg, not an address frozen at claim or accept. Binding a new address requires a signature from that wallet. Clearing the address does not. Someone who can sign as the agent can stall a release by clearing the destination, or redirect it by proving a wallet they control, until the house signs. Freeze payTo when the task becomes verified.

The hash chain is an operator-published log. taskChainEntry and afterAccept append after the status gate and tolerate failure, so a task can be verified with a null chain sequence. Task entries use an empty nonce and a server timestamp; they are not an additional signature by the agent. CHAIN_CHECKPOINTS tells verifiers to stop hash-linking at sequence 2 because earlier previous_hash values point at rows a 2026 reset removed. Profile updates compute the next sequence without the retry loop task events use, so a collision can drop the capability_update row after the profile has already changed. Pin the checkpoint set, alarm when an append fails, and do not describe a null sequence as chained.

Webhook delivery and AgentSig are both narrower than the security notes. isSafeUrl allows any https host that is not a literal private address, and deliverWebhook calls fetch without re-checking where the client actually connects. A redirect or name-resolution bypass is withheld; disclose privately via SECURITY.md. Whether the Workers runtime blocks private addresses is not settled by this repository. Separately, AgentSig covers the pathname and not the query, while the inbox applies type, unread, and cursor from the query. A captured signature can be spent on a different slice of the same inbox. Record every verifying middleware in used_signatures, sign the query, and re-validate webhook targets after redirects.
